evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost

criteria.reasoning: All four required items addressed in detail: primary mission, need (bleaching statistics, [1]-[3]), single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers clearly identified. Well referenced with literature. Only minor point: rationale for one satellite could quantify revisit trade vs constellation, but Section 2.3 covers this.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission

criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: launch site/vehicle with justified trade table and azimuth calculation, orbit elements (Table 4) with correct J2 sun-synchronous derivation, explicit no-manoeuvre statement, STK access table for ground station, data budget, 5-year duration and drag-sail EOL. Hand calculations verified correct (decay, azimuth, spacing, data volume). STK screenshots and files provided. Link budget admittedly missing.

evidence.quote: The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown
a 4 m² drag sail removes the satellite in about two years, compared with about 32 years without it

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are specific and quantitative, summarising orbit, coverage, communications and EOL results, and honestly identify four limitations with concrete next-phase actions. Well beyond generic.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat
The Space Review, article 3887 on drag sails for de-orbiting satellites.

criteria.reasoning: Clear logical structure with executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures/tables, and all in-text citations [1]-[15] matching the reference list. Writing is professional. Minor flaws: references [4] and [15] lack proper article titles/authors, and some figures (STK 3D views) are low-information content.

requirements.where: Images 1-5; Appendix A lists STK files in ZYZZsat_STK.zip

technical_issues.issue: Assumes S-band/X-band equipment can be added to the Mount Pleasant radio astronomy antenna; no link budget performed (acknowledged by student).
Vega C unflown at time of writing; fallback considered, but release altitude uncertainty propagates to orbit design (acknowledged).
References [4] and [15] incompletely specified (no article title/author).
Eclipse duration of ~34 min stated without shown calculation, though plausible for 600 km SSO.

overall: Excellent, comprehensive mission design report. All task requirements met with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and files, honest limitations, and professional presentation. Minor deductions for missing link budget, contingent launch vehicle, and two incomplete references.
